newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Missed phone call costs New World dear.
newsitem.headline: Missed phone call costs New World dear.

text.p: A missed phone call to suspend its shares from trading cost New World Development HK$30 million (US$3.85 million) during last Thursday's HK$2.78 billion share placement, a newspaper said on Saturday.
Officials from the company were not available for comment.

The South China Morning Post quoted market sources as saying New World was forced to accept a lower placement price after the stock traded for 13 minutes during the afternoon because nobody remembered to call the Stock Exchange to request a suspension.

Dramatic movements in the New World share price changed the placement price from an intended HK$37.50 to HK$37.10 during the extra 13 minutes of afternoon trading, the paper quoted its sources as saying.
As a result, New World got HK$0.40 per share less than if trading had stopped at the lunchtime close, the paper said.
The bourse finally received the call after lunch, in the early afternoon, and acted on the request.
